# pmon_workload_binding (Resource)

Maps a workload's OIDC token to a pmon service principal.

A service with no human behind it -- an AWS role (through IAM outbound identity federation), a GitHub Actions job, an HCP Terraform run -- exchanges the short-lived token its platform issues at pmon's `/api/workload/exchange`. pmon verifies it against a trusted issuer and mints a credential for the one enabled binding whose `subject` and every `conditions` entry match: a wire token for SQL through the proxy, an MCP access token, or either.

The principal holds roles like anyone else; grant them with `pmon_role_assignment`. Disabling, deleting, or narrowing a binding revokes every token it minted.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pmon_workload_binding" "settlement_batch" {
  name     = "settlement-batch"
  issuer   = "aws-prod"
  subject  = "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/settlement-batch"
  purposes = ["wire"]
  conditions = {
    "principal_tags.kubernetes-namespace"       = ["batch"]
    "principal_tags.kubernetes-service-account" = ["settlement"]
  }
}

resource "pmon_role_assignment" "settlement_batch" {
  principal = pmon_workload_binding.settlement_batch.principal
  role_name = "service:settlement"
}

resource "pmon_workload_binding" "pmon_plan" {
  name       = "tf-pmon-plan"
  issuer     = "hcp-terraform"
  subject    = "organization:acme:project:infra:workspace:pmon:run_phase:plan"
  principal  = "svc:tf-pmon"
  purposes   = ["mcp"]
  mcp_scopes = ["mcp:read"]
}

resource "pmon_workload_binding" "pmon_apply" {
  name       = "tf-pmon-apply"
  issuer     = "hcp-terraform"
  subject    = "organization:acme:project:infra:workspace:pmon:run_phase:apply"
  principal  = "svc:tf-pmon"
  purposes   = ["mcp"]
  mcp_scopes = ["mcp:read", "mcp:policies:write", "mcp:identity:write"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `issuer` (String) Name of a trusted issuer configured on pmon (`PM_CI_OIDC_ISSUERS`), for example `aws-prod`, `github`, or `hcp-terraform`.
- `name` (String) Binding name: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Changing it replaces the binding.
- `purposes` (Set of String) What an exchange may mint: `wire` (a SQL wire token) and `mcp` (an MCP access token).
- `subject` (String) The token's exact `sub`, or a prefix ending in `*`. An AWS token's `sub` is the IAM role ARN with its path; a GitHub Actions token's is `repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:<env>`; an HCP Terraform token's is `organization:<org>:project:<project>:workspace:<workspace>:run_phase:<plan|apply>`.

### Optional

- `conditions` (Map of Set of String) Claims that must also hold, as claim name to accepted values (each exact, or a prefix ending in `*`). Nested claims join their keys with a dot and AWS's own claims sit at the top level, for example `aws_account`, `principal_tags.kubernetes-namespace`, `repository`, or `terraform_run_phase`.
- `description` (String) What the workload is. Shown in pmon's console.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the binding matches tokens. Disabling it revokes what it minted.
- `mcp_scopes` (Set of String) The most an `mcp` exchange may carry. Required when `purposes` contains `mcp`, empty otherwise. Valid scopes are `mcp:approvals:write`, `mcp:datasources:write`, `mcp:identity:write`, `mcp:policies:write`, `mcp:query`, `mcp:read`, `mcp:tokens`.
- `principal` (String) Service principal the token acts as, `svc:<name>`. Defaults to `svc:` followed by the binding name.
- `ttl_seconds` (Number) Lifetime of a minted token, 60 to 3600 seconds. An MCP token is also capped by pmon's MCP access token lifetime.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) pmon's internal id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import pmon_workload_binding.settlement_batch settlement-batch
```
